title: Controlled Natural Language for Requirements Specification: A Systematic Literature Review
abstract: arXiv:2611.23259v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Requirements are critical artifacts of the software development life-cycle. They express capabilities that the system should provide, guiding both the development and testing process. Given their significance, require- ments specification has attracted the interest of researchers and practitioners in recent years. Requirements specification is an activity where requirements are specified, i.e., documented. In this context, Controlled Natural Languages (CNL) were proposed as a compromise between the ambiguity of natural language and the complexity of formal languages. CNLs enable the specification of requirements using accurate statements that can be processed automatically, while remaining understandable by stakeholders. In this article, we perform a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) to identify, categorize, and compare CNL approaches for requirements specification. translated_title: 用于需求规约的受控自然语言：一项系统性文献综述
translated_abstract: arXiv:2611.23259v1 公告类型：新论文 摘要：需求是软件开发生命周期中的关键产物。它们表达了系统应具备的能力，对开发和测试过程都起到指导作用。鉴于其重要性，需求规约近年来引起了研究人员和从业者的广泛关注。需求规约是一项对需求进行规约（即文档化）的活动。在此背景下，受控自然语言（CNL）被提出，作为自然语言的歧义性与形式语言的复杂性之间的一种折中方案。CNL 使人们能够使用可被自动处理的准确语句来规约需求，同时仍能被利益相关者所理解。在本文中，我们开展了一项系统性文献综述（SLR），以识别、分类并比较用于需求规约的 CNL 方法。该综述涵盖了 2000 年至 2024 年间发表的 133 篇原始研究。我们……
tldr: 本文通过一项覆盖2000年至2024年间133篇原始研究的系统性文献综述，对用于需求规约的受控自然语言（CNL）方法进行了识别、分类与比较。
en_tdlr: This paper conducts a Systematic Literature Review covering 133 primary studies published between 2000 and 2024 to identify, categorize, and compare Controlled Natural Language (CNL) approaches for requirements specification.
